body.statement: On the shared circular perfect-intervention setting, Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:perfect\text{-}intervention\text{-}family}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}grouping}\) retain the node-target intervention structure used by Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:density\text{-}smoothness}\), \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}smoothness}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}conditioning}\) strictly strengthen their qualitative envelopes for uniform rates. Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}cardinality}\), \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}separation}\), \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}attainment}\) replace an almost-everywhere nonzero discrepancy by a quantitative isolated-zero condition, which implies nonzero discrepancy almost everywhere. Consequently, at \(D_H=0\) the proposed quotient conclusion agrees with their componentwise exact-identification conclusion on the shared subclass; the new claim concerns only the nonzero-error rate.
body.justification: A theorem-level hypothesis map distinguishes inherited exact identification from the strengthened assumptions that buy a uniform modulus.
body.gap: The comparator papers establish exact recovery but do not separate which of their assumptions control identification and which additional envelopes would control a law-based rate.
body.consumer: Referees and users can identify precisely when the modulus specializes to the published exact results and what extra regularity is paid for quantitative stability.
